name: IRD mCCT Value of information for evaluation BOTEC
summary: Funds an evaluation of mobile cash incentives for child vaccination in Sindh, Pakistan. GiveWell's spreadsheet "IRD mCCT Value of information for evaluation BOTEC", linked from its grant page. Every number is traced from the sheet's bottom line; calculated rows reproduce the sheet's own values.

rows.label: How many years would we fund IRD's mCCT program if it met our bar for cost-effectiveness?
rows.explainer: Guess

rows.label: Probability of this scenario
rows.explainer: Guess. We guess there's a 65% chance we'd put substantial weight on the results and a 25% chance that these results would provide a negative update on cost-effectiveness. This gets us to roughly 15% (65% x 25%).

rows.label: Low-coverage districts in Sindh (Scenario 0: No evaluation)
High-coverage districts in Sindh (Scenario 0: No evaluation)
rows.explainer: This is a rough guess. We expect cost-effectiveness to be lower in districts with high counterfactual vaccination coverage. Because coverage is already high in these districts without incentives, there are more infants who would be vaccinated regardless (which implies higher costs) and fewer infants who could be induced to receive vaccinations as a result of incentives (which implies lower benefit).

rows.label: High-coverage districts in Sindh
rows.explainer: This is based on our estimate of RFMF in low-coverage districts and IRD's budget estimates to provide incentives to all of Sindh (~$12m). We subtract the amount going to low-coverage districts (~$6m) to get a best guess of ~$6m.

Cost-effectiveness of evaluation (multiplies of cash transfers from GiveDirectly)
Units of value per dollar given to GiveDirectly
rows.explainer: GiveWell reports this model's result in multiples of cash transfers. Multiplying by GiveWell's value of a dollar to GiveDirectly converts it into units of value per dollar, so it ranks against the other models. Older sheets used older moral weights; the multiple of cash is the comparable number across years.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for research, technical assistance and policy work: mostly people. Our judgment; we haven't seen this grant's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Researchers and advisers could typically earn considerably more in consulting or industry. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).
